text: Ask icedLiquid about the weather in Hamburg, and it answers out loud. The ears, the brain and the voice run on the laptop GPU, inside one Chrome tab.
One tab, the model from cache, one turn end to end, tools and cards, barge-in and the stage, the measured session, the limits, how to reproduce, and a thank you.
The page: one model line, a Start button, four pipeline tiles and a GPU line. The credit line under the conversation thanks Liquid AI.
LFM3-Omni does three jobs. The ears transcribe on the browser lane, the brain writes the reply, and the voice streams speech.
Your audio never leaves the tab. Only tool calls reach the web server, and the tool keys stay there.
In the recorded session the model loaded from the browser cache in 1477.3 milliseconds.
caption: In the recorded session the model loaded from the browser cache in 1477.3 ms.

text: The first visit downloads the weights once. Later visits read them from the cache. This manual quotes only the cached load.
One turn. You speak, and the ears in the browser turn your words into a final transcript for the agent.
The agent checks its phrase lists first. Then the brain thinks with the history and the tool specs, for up to 2 tool rounds.
A tool call goes to the web server. The result comes back as data and a card, and the brain answers from it.
Then the voice speaks the answer while it streams. Speak over it, and barge-in stops the answer and listens again.
The weather question. The tool returns data, the page draws a card, and the spoken answer is built from the same data.
One earlier live call each: weather in 212 milliseconds, time in 128 milliseconds, and web search in 3170 milliseconds.
caption: One earlier live call each: weather in 212 ms, time in 128 ms, and web search in 3170 ms.

text: Each tool feeds a card. Search lists 3 sources. The image tool is configured, but this session did not use it.
Barge-in is on in the config. Your voice must hold for 300 milliseconds and be louder than the echo of the answer.
Theme, goodbye and language switches come from phrase lists in the config, not from the model. A small model does not call those tools reliably.
Barge-in is configured, not measured in this run. Speakers can trigger it with the assistant's own voice, so use headphones.
Full screen fills the display with the orb, the tiles and the conversation, in light or dark. The session chips count turns, tokens and context.
On a phone the same tiles and chips stack in one column, and the GPU line wraps instead of cutting off.
12 answered turns. The median reply starts 1121.1 milliseconds after the question, the slow tail 2976.0 milliseconds.

text: Every badge is a measurement. The tiles time each stage, the badges count context, tokens, rate and tool rounds, and Save run exports them.
Context grew from 1150 tokens on the first turn to 1491 on the last. Every median includes the typed and the mic turns.
Browser microphone recognition is in diagnosis. Live, it returned text in 0 of 7 passes. A replay bench reached a non-empty share of 1.00, still an open gap.

text: The scripted questions were typed. Short unscripted microphone turns came from echo or room noise, and they stay in every median. One machine, one session.
Asked for the time in Tokyo, it answered without the time tool, and it was wrong. The config now has a grounding guard, not yet measured live.
Provision the browser weights once, start the web app, run a session and press Save run. The judge rebuilds every median from the saved turns.
Then check every number against the register with the claims checker. A different number is a finding, not a failure.
Thank you to the team at Liquid AI. LFM3-Omni listens, thinks and speaks in one model, small enough for a browser tab. Learn more at liquid dot A I.
